questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go somewhere outside of Europe where I had never been before and I have always wanted to go to Australia.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were several orientation days and we always had the opportunity to contact our study abroad advisor at USYD if we had any questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quite hard to find something close to the university that had a somewhat reasonable price. Especially since we were two who wanted to live together. It seemed easier to find a place for just one person.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I think it was great living off campus. I lived close to both the university and other interesting areas of the city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Housing in Sydney is very expensive!

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: If you are going on exchange in semester 1 of your master's degree and finished your bachelor's degree just before starting your master's degree you may not be able to choose postgraduate courses at USYD. I had this problem since the deadline for uploading proof of completion of my bachelor's degree was before my last bachelor's exam.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have to choose courses when sending your application to USYD but you can change your courses all the way up to the end of the first week of classes. You can even have a say in what your timetable will look like as you can request certain time slots for each class.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We could always contact our study abroad advisor and we could even book a meeting if necessary.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: On USYD's website it says that OLET courses are available for exchange students. However, that turned out to be untrue. Apart from the OLET courses that I wanted, I was successful in registering for the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: As long as you keep an eye out for emails about deadlines you will have no problems with registration.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I chose courses on many different levels. All of them were at a good level - not too easy and not too difficult.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There were a lot more students enrolled in all of my courses than what is usually the case at UCPH. The teaching was therefore less personal than what I am used to. The teaching style is also more like in Danish high schools than Danish universities with compulsory attendance in classes and more assignments that also count towards the final grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Computational Chemistry
Learning in Outdoor Education
Australian Wildlife Biology
Introduction to Indigenous History

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you are interested in learning about Australia I would definitely recommend Learning in Outdoor Education and Australian Wildlife Biology. In Learning in Outdoor Education you learn about bush walking and being in nature and you get to go on a one day trip to Royal National Park and a three day trip to the Blue Mountains. In Australian Wildlife Biology you learn about lots of different Australian animals and I found this very interesting and useful, especially when I travelled around Australia after the end of the semester.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Transportation was cheaper than expected. Housing was a lot more expensive than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Lots of different clubs and societies so there is something for everyone. The student union also offers lots of activities, events and trips.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend taking part in some of the free activities and trips that are arranged by the student union (USU) and they also have some events you can attend for a small fee. Sign up for some clubs as well - they may have some interesting events and even if they don't chances are that they will have free food.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel as much as you can! There are so many incredible places all around Australia. The Blue Mountains (just outside of Sydney) is a great place to spend a weekend hiking in the mountains. The botanical garden is great as well.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy since Australia is quite ‘European'. Of course there were differences but not anything that was hard to adjust to.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Choose courses that are not only meant for international students and sign up for the Mates Abroad program.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Australians are very polite and easy to talk to. I found the Aboriginal culture very interesting and fascinating.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
It might seem like a huge step to move to another country (and it is!) but it is not as scary and difficult when you get here as you may think. I arrived in Sydney almost two weeks before the main orientation day and almost three weeks before classes began and I think that it was a great decision. It gave me time to figure out everything and explore the city before I had to focus on university.

If you have the opportunity try to choose some units of study that are different from what you would choose at home. Being on exchange is a great chance to try something new and learn about the place where you will be living for some months.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure you get a Concession Opal Card for public transportation in and around Sydney so that all of your journeys will be half price.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living in another country for a quite long period of time, meeting new people and experiencing many parts of the country after the semester ended.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To be honest I did not really encounter any challenges but if I have to mention one it would probably be figuring out the right balance between doing good at the university while still taking enough time to explore and enjoy the city and Australia in general.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
